items.item_text: This position requires a minimum of two (2) days/week on campus/on-site.
Job offer is contingent upon satisfactory clearance based on Background Check results.
Occasional evenings and weekends may be required.

Mandated reporter under CANRA. Duties may require direct contact with children (defined as individuals under the age of 18). Completion of the Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act (CANRA) form will be required.
Cover letter required for a complete application.

Knowledge of human resources management systems and other related business software programs and systems. Experience with UCPath or other payroll/HR systems and ability to use data processing software and relational database systems to process full range of personnel actions (recruitment, timekeeping, increases, funding changes, etc.).

Demonstrated ability, past experience to solve complex problems through the creative ability to identify, construct, evaluate, and implement innovative and sound solutions to a wide range of issues. Requires ability to use initiative, creativity and resourcefulness to accomplish projects and tasks at hand.

Demonstrated knowledge and hands-on experience managing international scholar services, including proficiency in visa procedures (e.g., J-1, H-1B, OPT/STEM OPT), policies, immigration laws pertaining to foreign scholars, appointment workflows and onboarding.

Reporting to the Academic Personnel Manager, the incumbent supports day-to-day academic personnel operations for engineering departments. This role provides guidance to department leadership on issues of moderate scope and complexity.

The incumbent delivers AP services across recruitment, reviews, compensation, classification, affirmative action, merit reviews, Leaves of Absences (LOA)/ Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA), workplace accommodations, worker’s compensation, visa procurement and separations/layoffs. Additionally, this role executes all personnel transactions in UCPath, including appointments, salary adjustments, reclassifications, and separations, while ensuring precise payroll funding, managing personnel records and leading onboarding and offboarding from start to end. The position interprets university academic policies, assists in providing guidance on labor contracts, sensitive disciplinary actions, enforces affirmative action compliance, and liaises directly with the Academic Personnel Manager, AP Team Leads and central campus offices on complex matters.

The incumbent applies Academic HR concepts, organization and UC-wide policies and procedures to provide guidance to Department Chairs, CAO, faculty and staff to resolve a wide variety of academic HR issues of moderate scope and complexity. As a position that serves one or more established areas, the AP analyst is the first point of contact for many issues and has the autonomy to make recommendations and triage decisions within the parameters of the Dean's Office standard practices and procedures. Department assignments is subject to review and redistribution as necessary to support the Jacobs School of Engineering.
Oversee special projects and other duties as assigned. Provide backup support to other team members.
~ Cover letter required for a complete application.
Basic knowledge of and ability to apply / interpret organization and college policies and procedures which govern academic HR.

Knowledge of organization, college and departmental formal and informal policies and procedures and understanding of variances to stated policies. Skill to see the comprehensive picture both in terms of current complexities and interactions and in the required long- range view over time. Knowledge and understanding of the structure of large organizations and how to effectively operate to accomplish goals and develop new initiatives/programs within this framework.
Ability to communicate database requirements and goals to programming staff. Ability to conceptualize, develop and utilize new systems, reports and tools for data retrieval, analysis and review.
Knowledge of unit academic culture and educational goals of discipline(s) served.
Analytical skills to conduct analysis and develop recommendations to Chairs / unit management.

Demonstrated organization, problem solving, and communication skills. Proven analytical skills used in evaluating information, procedures or situations to define a problem or objective, identify relevant concerns, recognize alternatives, formulate logical and objective conclusions and prepare reports, suggest solutions, etc. Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to communicate and interact with a diverse group of individuals from within and outside the university, using tact, diplomacy, and sensitivity; ability to develop and maintain good working relationships with employees, faculty, managers, supervisors and campus administrators. Ability to explain policies, procedures, and other concepts in easily understandable terms.
Knowledge of appointment/review process for university academic employees.

Knowledge of policies and procedures as they relate to academic personnel, benefits and payroll administration. Including university pay scales, salary administration, benefits, payroll system and payroll forms related to academic affairs and academic personnel. Excellent mathematical and computational skills to work with percentages and formulas.
Knowledge of academic appointment and employment policies.

Ability to work independently and resourcefully against deadlines exercising a high degree of judgment, discreetly and confidentiality to accomplish assignments. Demonstrated ability to set priorities, see tasks through from start to completion in order to meet deadlines, despite frequent interruptions.

Ability to maintain confidentiality, make independent decisions, and to provide consultative services to administrative and academic personnel. Ability to work with little supervision and with initiative, including aptitude to repeat routine tasks without reminders. Proven Ability to manage a large volume of detailed work.

Skill in analyzing situations/issues and making recommendations or proposals for management decisions. Demonstrated ability to collect data, anticipate and resolve problems, evaluate possibilities of alternative solutions.
Skill in developing and efficiently maintaining accurate record keeping systems.

Demonstrated proficiency with business software including word processing, spreadsheets, email and calendaring systems. Demonstrated ability to learn and use specialized or proprietary systems and applications and the ability to update and expand skills as needed.
Willingness and demonstrated ability to embrace and consistently uphold the principles of community for a collaborative work environment.
Ability to use project management platforms (such as ClickUp) to streamline HR workflows, track deliverables, ensure accountability and optimize operations.
